prompt: Humans can biosynthesize all eight essential monosaccharides from simpler precursors. Why is it still better to obtain them from the diet?

choices.text: It is more energetically efficient
The body can make only the L forms, and the D forms are needed
choices.why: The body can biosynthesize all eight if necessary. Getting them from food simply costs less energy.

choices.text: Biosynthesis from simpler precursors is impossible in humans
choices.why: The section says all eight can be biosynthesized if necessary.

choices.text: Dietary sugars are already linked into glycoconjugates
choices.why: The reason the section gives is energy efficiency, not the form the sugars arrive in.

explanation: Humans need eight monosaccharides for proper functioning. Although all eight can be biosynthesized from simpler precursors if necessary, it is more energetically efficient to obtain them from the diet.

prompt: What are all eight essential monosaccharides used for?

choices.text: Synthesis of the glycoconjugate components of cell membranes
Only as fuel, since they are the body's energy source
choices.why: Glucose is also the body's primary energy source, but all eight are used to make glycoconjugates of cell membranes.

choices.text: Building cellulose for structural support in cell walls
choices.why: Cellulose is a plant structural material. The essential monosaccharides are used for glycoconjugates in cell membranes.

choices.text: Long-term energy storage in the form of glycogen
choices.why: The use the section names for all eight is synthesis of the glycoconjugate components of cell membranes.

explanation: All eight essential monosaccharides are used for the synthesis of the glycoconjugate components of cell membranes, and glucose is also the body's primary source of energy.

prompt: How many of the eight essential monosaccharides does the section describe as simple aldohexoses?
explanation: Galactose, glucose, and mannose are simple aldohexoses. Xylose is an aldopentose, fucose is a deoxy sugar, N-acetylglucosamine and N-acetylgalactosamine are amide derivatives of amino sugars, and N-acetylneuraminic acid has nine carbons.

prompt: L-Fucose is 6-deoxy-L-galactose. What makes it a deoxy sugar?

choices.text: The –OH group at carbon 6 is replaced by an –H
The –OH group at carbon 2 is replaced by an –NH2 group
choices.why: That describes the amino sugars behind N-acetylglucosamine and N-acetylgalactosamine.

choices.text: The –OH group at carbon 2 is replaced by an –H
choices.why: The 6- in 6-deoxy-L-galactose shows that the missing oxygen is at carbon 6.

choices.text: It has no ring oxygen
choices.why: A deoxy sugar has an oxygen atom "missing" because an –OH is replaced by –H, not because the ring lacks oxygen.

explanation: Fucose is a deoxy sugar, meaning that it has an oxygen atom "missing." That is, an –OH group (the one at carbon 6) is replaced by an –H.

prompt: What kind of compound is N-acetyl-D-glucosamine?

choices.text: An amide of an amino sugar, with –NH2 in place of the carbon 2 –OH
A deoxy sugar in which the –OH at carbon 6 is replaced by an –H
choices.why: That describes L-fucose.

choices.text: An ester of glucose with acetic acid at the anomeric –OH
choices.why: The acetyl group is on nitrogen, forming an amide, not on an oxygen.

choices.text: A nine-carbon parent compound of the sialic acids
choices.why: That is N-acetylneuraminic acid.

explanation: N-Acetylglucosamine and N-acetylgalactosamine are amide derivatives of amino sugars in which an –OH (the one at carbon 2) is replaced by an –NH2 group.

prompt: N-Acetylneuraminic acid is the parent compound of which group of compounds?

choices.text: The sialic acids, more than 30 compounds
The deoxy sugars, such as L-fucose
choices.why: Deoxy sugars, such as fucose, have an –OH replaced by –H.

choices.text: The uronic acids, such as D-glucuronic acid
choices.why: Uronic acids are aldoses oxidized at the –CH2OH end, such as D-glucuronic acid.

choices.text: The aldaric acids, such as D-glucaric acid
choices.why: Aldaric acids are dicarboxylic acids made from aldoses with HNO3.

explanation: N-Acetylneuraminic acid is the parent compound of the sialic acids, a group of more than 30 compounds with different modifications, including various oxidations, acetylations, sulfations, and methylations.

prompt: How many carbon atoms does neuraminic acid have?
explanation: Neuraminic acid has nine carbons. It is an aldol reaction product of N-acetylmannosamine with pyruvate (CH3COCO2−).

choices.text: By an aldol reaction of N-acetylmannosamine with pyruvate, CH3COCO2−
By Kiliani–Fischer chain extension of N-acetylglucosamine
choices.why: Kiliani–Fischer adds one carbon to an aldose; the section describes neuraminic acid as an aldol product.

choices.text: By glycoside formation between N-acetylmannosamine and pyruvate
choices.why: A glycoside is an acetal at the anomeric carbon. Neuraminic acid comes from an aldol reaction, which makes a C–C bond.

choices.text: By oxidation of N-acetylgalactosamine with warm, dilute HNO3
choices.why: HNO3 oxidation gives aldaric acids. Neuraminic acid comes from an aldol reaction of N-acetylmannosamine with pyruvate.

explanation: Neuraminic acid has nine carbons and is an aldol reaction product of N-acetylmannosamine with pyruvate (CH3COCO2−), as Exercise 25.7.1 asks you to show.

prompt: Neuraminic acid is crucial to which process?

choices.text: The mechanism by which an influenza virus spreads
Energy storage in animals
choices.why: Energy storage in animals is the job of glycogen.

choices.text: Recognition of sweetness by taste receptors
choices.why: The section links neuraminic acid to the spread of influenza virus.

choices.text: Copying DNA
choices.why: DNA contains the deoxy sugar 2-deoxyribose, not neuraminic acid.

explanation: Neuraminic acid is crucial to the mechanism by which an influenza virus spreads.

prompt: From which compound do all eight essential monosaccharides arise in biosynthesis?

choices.text: Glucose
Pyruvate
choices.why: Pyruvate joins N-acetylmannosamine to make neuraminic acid, but all eight essential monosaccharides arise from glucose.

choices.text: Galactose
choices.why: Galactose is itself one of the eight, made from glucose.

choices.text: Xylose
choices.why: Xylose is itself one of the eight, made from glucose.

explanation: All the essential monosaccharides arise from glucose, by the conversions summarized in Figure 25.7.2; mannose and fucose are made by way of fructose.
